sections.html:
Oconee County is compact and part of the Athens-Clarke County metro area, with Watkinsville as the seat. Its population went from 32,808 in 2010 to 41,799 in 2020, and the July 2025 estimate is 44,893. Owners occupy 81.3% of the homes, and a typical one carries a value of $461,600. Expect buyers in this price range to scrutinize the tax history.

Four towns appear on the map: Bishop, Bogart, North High Shoals and Watkinsville. Elder, Farmington and Salem are unincorporated and have no town government. Inside a town limit there may be a separate municipal bill, so find out where your parcel sits.

sections.h2: Who bills and who values property?
sections.html:
A bill and a valuation come from two different desks. The Tax Commissioner is at 7635 Macon Highway in Watkinsville, with mail going to Suite 300. Counter hours are weekdays from 8:00 until 4:30. Call (706) 769-3917 or text (706) 765-7790.

  • Tax Assessors, (706) 769-3921: values, returns, exemptions
  • Board of Commissioners and Board of Education: each adopts a mill rate
  • Courthouse record center, 23 North Main Street, (706) 769-3940: copies of warranty deeds

Nearly 70% of a tax bill funds schools and the rest funds county government. The appraisal staff handle value only. The tax amount follows from the millage the two boards set. School zoning is a district decision, so ask the school district which school an address feeds before you describe it to buyers.

Assessors fix a fair market value as of January 1. Taxable (assessed) value is 40% of it. One mill equals one dollar of tax for every $1,000 of that taxable figure. The Board of Commissioners adopts a mill rate for county government and the Board of Education adopts one for schools. Your bill is the assessed value, less any exemption, times the combined rate.

The appraisal staff calculate values for real estate, marine, aircraft and business personal property in a computer-assisted mass appraisal system, and the appraisers hold state certification at four levels. That means your value comes from a model applied to every parcel, not a visit to your house, so photos and repair estimates help if you think the model missed a defect.

Four commissioners and a separately elected chairman, all chosen countywide for staggered four-year terms, hold the budget, taxing and ordinance powers. The chairman is the chief executive. If you want to speak to the boards that set the rate, those are the officials who vote on it each year.

Business personal property and real estate bills are normally payable by November 15. Mobile home tax is payable by April 1.

  • Interest: bank prime rate plus 3 points a year, divided by 12 and applied monthly, with the state announcing the year's rate on or after January 1
  • Penalty: 5% of principal every 120 days past due, topping out at 20%
  • Enforcement: an unpaid account lets the Tax Commissioner levy on the property
  • Payment plans: set up by phone once bills are mailed, with interest and penalties still running until the balance is paid

Interest moves every month, so an old figure may fall short by closing day. Get the payoff figure on paper before you sell.

Your assessment notice prints the filing deadline in its upper right corner, under the words last date to file a written appeal. That date sits 45 days past the notice date. A letter or the county's appeal form will do, but an emailed or online filing will not.

Keep your evidence simple: a recent appraisal, sales of similar nearby homes, and photos of problems. Write the parcel number and your reason on the letter and keep a copy.

You may go to the Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator. After that ruling, a written notice sent to the assessors carries the case to superior court. Appraisal staff rule on value only, never on the size of the bill.

To qualify you must own the house and live in it on January 1, and the application has to arrive before April 1. Valuation is frozen as of January 1, so a renovation or demolition during the year counts from the next January 1. Call the assessors at (706) 769-3921 for current exemption amounts.

Nothing carries over automatically. The exemption belongs to the current owner. A buyer who will live in the house needs to file their own application, so mention the April 1 date during the sale.

sections.h2: What should a seller sort out before closing?
sections.html:
Both ownership and condition are fixed as of January 1, which means a bill is still waiting to be divided when a house sells midyear. Put the split in the contract.

  • Request a payoff from the Tax Commissioner and hand a copy to the closing agent
  • Pull a copy of the warranty deed at the courthouse record center when the legal description is needed
  • Check whether the parcel is in unincorporated Oconee County or inside Watkinsville, Bishop, Bogart or North High Shoals, since a town may bill its own tax
  • Wrap up any open appeal before closing so a pending value cannot stall a refund

Refund claims for tax assessed in error have a three-year clock from payment. If a wrong value led you to overpay, ask the assessors about a correction rather than waiting, and keep the closing statement as proof of what was paid and when. If you overpaid at closing because of a wrong value, ask the assessors about a correction rather than waiting, and keep the closing statement as proof of what was paid and when.

An unpaid November 15 bill keeps growing while the house is listed, with a 5% penalty at each 120 day mark up to 20%. Ask the Tax Commissioner for a written payoff dated near the closing day.

The closing agent pays it out of your sale proceeds and forwards it to the commissioner. Mention any payment plan to the agent, since a plan does not stop interest. A cash sale avoids the lender's tax review and appraisal wait, which can matter when time is short and an old balance is sitting on the account.

Also confirm your homestead was filed before the April 1 cutoff this year. A missed filing is hard to repair later, and the buyer's lender will review the tax figures when underwriting the loan.

faqs.q: What is the normal property tax due date in Oconee County?
faqs.a: Real estate and business personal property are due November 15 and mobile homes April 1. Charges begin to accrue after the date.

faqs.q: What is the last day to appeal an Oconee County value?
faqs.a: It is printed on the notice itself, 45 days after the notice date. The appraisal office will not accept an appeal filed electronically.

faqs.q: Which boards set the millage rate in Oconee County?
faqs.a: Two bodies: the Board of Commissioners for county government and the Board of Education for schools. A mill means a dollar of tax per $1,000 of assessed value, with assessed value set at 40% of market value.

faqs.q: How much does Oconee County charge for late property tax?
faqs.a: Monthly interest at prime plus 3% a year, and then a 5% penalty at each 120-day mark until penalties total 20% of principal.

faqs.q: Which towns are in Oconee County?
faqs.a: Four: Bishop, Bogart, North High Shoals and Watkinsville, the seat. Elder, Farmington and Salem have no town government.
